paragraphs.source_en: Morever, even if we somehow managed to get our hands on a macro scopic wormhole, we wouldn't be done; we'd still face a couple of significant obstacles. First, in the 1 960s, Wheeler and Robert Fuller showed, using the equations of general relativity, that wormholes are unstable. Their walls tend to collapse inward in a fraction of a second, which elim inates their utility for any kind of travel. More recently, though, physicists (including Thorne and Morris, and also Matt Visser) have found a potential way around the collapse problem. If the wormhole is not empty, but instead contains material -so-called exotic matter - that can exert an out ward push on its walls, then it might be possible to keep the wormhole open and stable.
